      Use Sprites with Meta (Muse Spark)
      
    </h3>
    <a href="https://fly.io/dashboard" class="inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 font-mono text-xs text-navy-500 hover:text-violet-700 transition-colors" rel="noopener" target="_blank">
      fly.io/dashboard
      <span class="hero-arrow-top-right-on-square-mini w-3.5 h-3.5 text-navy-300"></span>
    </a>
  </div>

  <p class="mt-2 text-sm text-navy-600">Call Muse Spark from a Sprite while keeping your Meta API key outside the environment.</p>
  

  <ol class="mt-5 divide-y divide-navy-100">
    <li class="grid grid-cols-[1.5rem_minmax(0,1fr)] sm:grid-cols-[2rem_minmax(0,1fr)] gap-x-3 sm:gap-x-4 py-4 first:pt-0 last:pb-0">
  <span class="text-xs sm:text-sm font-mono text-right leading-6 text-navy-400">
    1
  </span>

  <div class="flex flex-col gap-2 min-w-0">
    <p class="text-sm font-medium text-navy-700">Open your organization&#39;s Sprites Connectors</p>

    

    

    

    <p class="text-xs leading-relaxed text-navy-500">
      
      <span>In the Fly.io dashboard, select your organization, then open Sprites → Connectors → Add connector.</span>
    </p>
  </div>
</li><li class="grid grid-cols-[1.5rem_minmax(0,1fr)] sm:grid-cols-[2rem_minmax(0,1fr)] gap-x-3 sm:gap-x-4 py-4 first:pt-0 last:pb-0">
  <span class="text-xs sm:text-sm font-mono text-right leading-6 text-navy-400">
    2
  </span>

  <div class="flex flex-col gap-2 min-w-0">
    <p class="text-sm font-medium text-navy-700">Configure Meta</p>

    

    

    

    <p class="text-xs leading-relaxed text-navy-500">
      
      <span>Use your Meta developer team&#39;s API key. Availability varies by organization during rollout. The gateway keeps the credential off your Sprite.</span>
    </p>
  </div>
</li><li class="grid grid-cols-[1.5rem_minmax(0,1fr)] sm:grid-cols-[2rem_minmax(0,1fr)] gap-x-3 sm:gap-x-4 py-4 first:pt-0 last:pb-0">
  <span class="text-xs sm:text-sm font-mono text-right leading-6 text-navy-400">
    3
  </span>

  <div class="flex flex-col gap-2 min-w-0">
    <p class="text-sm font-medium text-navy-700">Grant your Sprite access</p>

    

    

    

    <p class="text-xs leading-relaxed text-navy-500">
      
      <span>Open access settings and turn off Allow all sprites before restricting access by name prefix or labels. If you set both, a Sprite must match both. Save the policy. A connector with no access policy denies all Sprites.</span>
    </p>
  </div>
</li><li class="grid grid-cols-[1.5rem_minmax(0,1fr)] sm:grid-cols-[2rem_minmax(0,1fr)] gap-x-3 sm:gap-x-4 py-4 first:pt-0 last:pb-0">
  <span class="text-xs sm:text-sm font-mono text-right leading-6 text-navy-400">
    4
  </span>

  <div class="flex flex-col gap-2 min-w-0">
    <p class="text-sm font-medium text-navy-700">Test from your Sprite</p>

    

    

    

    <p class="text-xs leading-relaxed text-navy-500">
      
      <span>Run the API Usage example from the connector&#39;s detail page inside an authorized Sprite. The gateway attaches the stored credential; do not copy it into the Sprite.</span>
    </p>
  </div>
</li>
  </ol>

  <p class="mt-5 text-xs leading-relaxed text-navy-500">
    Supports streaming and tool calls through OpenAI-compatible chat completions and responses, and Anthropic-compatible messages. The gateway also allows model discovery; other Meta API paths are blocked.
  </p>

      Use Sprites with OpenAI
      
    </h3>
    <a href="https://fly.io/dashboard" class="inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 font-mono text-xs text-navy-500 hover:text-violet-700 transition-colors" rel="noopener" target="_blank">
      fly.io/dashboard
      <span class="hero-arrow-top-right-on-square-mini w-3.5 h-3.5 text-navy-300"></span>
    </a>
  </div>

  <p class="mt-2 text-sm text-navy-600">Call OpenAI&#39;s Responses, Chat Completions and Embeddings APIs from a Sprite without an OpenAI key inside it.</p>
  

  <ol class="mt-5 divide-y divide-navy-100">
    <li class="grid grid-cols-[1.5rem_minmax(0,1fr)] sm:grid-cols-[2rem_minmax(0,1fr)] gap-x-3 sm:gap-x-4 py-4 first:pt-0 last:pb-0">
  <span class="text-xs sm:text-sm font-mono text-right leading-6 text-navy-400">
    1
  </span>

  <div class="flex flex-col gap-2 min-w-0">
    <p class="text-sm font-medium text-navy-700">Open your organization&#39;s Sprites Connectors</p>

    

    

    

    <p class="text-xs leading-relaxed text-navy-500">
      
      <span>In the Fly.io dashboard, select your organization, then open Sprites → Connectors → Add connector.</span>
    </p>
  </div>
</li><li class="grid grid-cols-[1.5rem_minmax(0,1fr)] sm:grid-cols-[2rem_minmax(0,1fr)] gap-x-3 sm:gap-x-4 py-4 first:pt-0 last:pb-0">
  <span class="text-xs sm:text-sm font-mono text-right leading-6 text-navy-400">
    2
  </span>

  <div class="flex flex-col gap-2 min-w-0">
    <p class="text-sm font-medium text-navy-700">Configure OpenAI</p>

    

    

    

    <p class="text-xs leading-relaxed text-navy-500">
      
      <span>Create a project API key at platform.openai.com. The gateway keeps the credential off your Sprite.</span>
    </p>
  </div>
</li><li class="grid grid-cols-[1.5rem_minmax(0,1fr)] sm:grid-cols-[2rem_minmax(0,1fr)] gap-x-3 sm:gap-x-4 py-4 first:pt-0 last:pb-0">
  <span class="text-xs sm:text-sm font-mono text-right leading-6 text-navy-400">
    3
  </span>

  <div class="flex flex-col gap-2 min-w-0">
    <p class="text-sm font-medium text-navy-700">Grant your Sprite access</p>

    

    

    

    <p class="text-xs leading-relaxed text-navy-500">
      
      <span>Open access settings and turn off Allow all sprites before restricting access by name prefix or labels. If you set both, a Sprite must match both. Save the policy. A connector with no access policy denies all Sprites.</span>
    </p>
  </div>
</li><li class="grid grid-cols-[1.5rem_minmax(0,1fr)] sm:grid-cols-[2rem_minmax(0,1fr)] gap-x-3 sm:gap-x-4 py-4 first:pt-0 last:pb-0">
  <span class="text-xs sm:text-sm font-mono text-right leading-6 text-navy-400">
    4
  </span>

  <div class="flex flex-col gap-2 min-w-0">
    <p class="text-sm font-medium text-navy-700">Test from your Sprite</p>

    

    

    

    <p class="text-xs leading-relaxed text-navy-500">
      
      <span>Run the API Usage example from the connector&#39;s detail page inside an authorized Sprite. The gateway attaches the stored credential; do not copy it into the Sprite.</span>
    </p>
  </div>
</li>
  </ol>

  <p class="mt-5 text-xs leading-relaxed text-navy-500">
    Requests are billed to your OpenAI project. Only /v1/responses, /v1/chat/completions, /v1/embeddings and /v1/models are forwarded; files, fine-tuning and organization paths are rejected.

      Use Sprites with SenseLab
      
    </h3>
    <a href="https://fly.io/dashboard" class="inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 font-mono text-xs text-navy-500 hover:text-violet-700 transition-colors" rel="noopener" target="_blank">
      fly.io/dashboard
      <span class="hero-arrow-top-right-on-square-mini w-3.5 h-3.5 text-navy-300"></span>
    </a>
  </div>

  <p class="mt-2 text-sm text-navy-600">Share agent memory, briefings and outcomes across disposable Sprites.</p>
  

  <ol class="mt-5 divide-y divide-navy-100">
    <li class="grid grid-cols-[1.5rem_minmax(0,1fr)] sm:grid-cols-[2rem_minmax(0,1fr)] gap-x-3 sm:gap-x-4 py-4 first:pt-0 last:pb-0">
  <span class="text-xs sm:text-sm font-mono text-right leading-6 text-navy-400">
    1
  </span>

  <div class="flex flex-col gap-2 min-w-0">

    <p class="text-xs leading-relaxed text-navy-500">
      
      <span>In the Fly.io dashboard, select your organization, then open Sprites → Connectors → Add connector.</span>
    </p>
  </div>
</li><li class="grid grid-cols-[1.5rem_minmax(0,1fr)] sm:grid-cols-[2rem_minmax(0,1fr)] gap-x-3 sm:gap-x-4 py-4 first:pt-0 last:pb-0">
  <span class="text-xs sm:text-sm font-mono text-right leading-6 text-navy-400">
    2
  </span>

  <div class="flex flex-col gap-2 min-w-0">
    <p class="text-sm font-medium text-navy-700">Configure SenseLab</p>

    

    

    

    <p class="text-xs leading-relaxed text-navy-500">
      
      <span>Create a non-admin API key in SenseLab Settings → API Keys. Replace the default * scope with the memory paths and read/write permissions your Sprites need. The gateway keeps the credential off your Sprite.</span>
    </p>
  </div>
</li><li class="grid grid-cols-[1.5rem_minmax(0,1fr)] sm:grid-cols-[2rem_minmax(0,1fr)] gap-x-3 sm:gap-x-4 py-4 first:pt-0 last:pb-0">
  <span class="text-xs sm:text-sm font-mono text-right leading-6 text-navy-400">
    3
  </span>

  <div class="flex flex-col gap-2 min-w-0">
    <p class="text-sm font-medium text-navy-700">Grant your Sprite access</p>

    

    

    

    <p class="text-xs leading-relaxed text-navy-500">
      
      <span>Open access settings and turn off Allow all sprites before restricting access by name prefix or labels. If you set both, a Sprite must match both. Save the policy. A connector with no access policy denies all Sprites.</span>
    </p>
  </div>
</li><li class="grid grid-cols-[1.5rem_minmax(0,1fr)] sm:grid-cols-[2rem_minmax(0,1fr)] gap-x-3 sm:gap-x-4 py-4 first:pt-0 last:pb-0">
  <span class="text-xs sm:text-sm font-mono text-right leading-6 text-navy-400">
    4
  </span>

  <div class="flex flex-col gap-2 min-w-0">
    <p class="text-sm font-medium text-navy-700">Test from your Sprite</p>

    

    

    

    <p class="text-xs leading-relaxed text-navy-500">
      
      <span>Run the API Usage example from the connector&#39;s detail page inside an authorized Sprite. The gateway attaches the stored credential; do not copy it into the Sprite.</span>
    </p>
  </div>
</li>
  </ol>

  <p class="mt-5 text-xs leading-relaxed text-navy-500">
    Admin keys are rejected. A non-admin key is not necessarily narrowly scoped: the default * scope can grant read/write access to every memory path. Authorized Sprites share the stored key&#39;s permissions; use separate scoped keys and connections for isolation. Agent and session IDs are provenance, not access controls. Saving, replacing and testing check key identity and admin status, not write permission. Requests use your SenseLab plan. Only supported memory operations are forwarded; no account administration, branch management, training or subscriptions. Your agent must explicitly read context and record findings and outcomes; the connector does not do this automatically.
  </p>

Project access is not isolated to a downstream account or user per Sprite: authorized Sprites can act on the connected accounts permitted by the project key. Tool execution can change external data and incur charges. A successful key check does not verify a particular account or tool-execution permission.

An approved spend request returns the virtual card&#39;s number, CVC and expiry to the Sprite so the agent can check out. Anyone who controls an allowed Sprite can read them. The card works once and expires after 12 hours. Each spend request is approved by the Link account owner in the Link app within 30 minutes. Sprites cannot approve their own requests. Link allows up to $500 per spend request, $500 per day and $20,000 per 30 days. Agent payments are available in the US and Canada; financial insights scopes are US only. A connection is one person&#39;s wallet. Use the access policy to limit it to that person&#39;s Sprites; other Sprites that are allowed can still create spend requests for the owner to approve.

  <p class="mt-5 text-xs leading-relaxed text-navy-500">
    Saving or testing a key lists at most one existing transcript (GET /v2/transcript?limit=1) and costs nothing. Every POST /v2/transcript is charged by AssemblyAI per hour of audio for the chosen speech model (AssemblyAI-STT-3.7 is priced per hour; see assemblyai.com/pricing), and add-ons such as speaker labels, PII redaction or speech understanding options in the request may cost extra. Polling GET /v2/transcript/:id is limited to 60 requests per minute per transcript. Forwards the pre-recorded speech-to-text API at api.assemblyai.com: POST /v2/upload, GET/POST /v2/transcript, GET/DELETE /v2/transcript/:id and its /sentences, /paragraphs, /srt, /vtt, /word-search and /redacted-audio routes. The EU host (api.eu.assemblyai.com), streaming speech-to-text (WebSocket), Sync, Dictation, Text-to-Speech, LLM Gateway and Speech Understanding over LLM Gateway are on other hosts and are not forwarded. Set speech_models to [&quot;assemblyai-stt-3-7&quot;] to pin the AssemblyAI-STT-3.7 model; it keeps disfluencies by default, so set disfluencies to false for clean text. DELETE /v2/transcript/:id removes the transcript&#39;s data and any file uploaded for it from AssemblyAI. Direct uploads above 8,000,000 bytes (8 MB) return HTTP 413. For larger recordings, send an audio_url that AssemblyAI can fetch.

  <p class="mt-5 text-xs leading-relaxed text-navy-500">
    Linear&#39;s API has no per-request charge. Saving or testing the key runs { viewer { id name } }, a one-field query about the key&#39;s own user. Linear rate limits each user to 2,500 requests and 3,000,000 complexity points per hour on standard plans (shared across all of that user&#39;s keys) and answers 429 with a Retry-After header when exceeded. The gateway forwards POST /graphql. Your key&#39;s Linear permissions and team restrictions determine which queries and mutations succeed. This includes requesting signed file upload URLs. A key with sufficient admin privileges can manage webhooks that send future workspace events to a configured URL. Manage or delete a registered webhook in Linear to stop delivery. OAuth flows, webhook deliveries and file uploads to signed URLs run outside this gateway route. Mutations create, update, archive and delete objects in your workspace and notify your teammates like any other change. Prefer a Read-only key unless the Sprite needs to write.
  </p>

  <p class="mt-5 text-xs leading-relaxed text-navy-500">
    Notion&#39;s API has no per-request charge. Saving or testing the token reads the token&#39;s bot user (GET /v1/users/me). Notion rate limits each connection to 180 requests per minute (600 on Business and Enterprise plans) and answers with 429 and a Retry-After header when exceeded. Forwards the Notion data APIs: users, search, pages (including /markdown and /move), blocks, databases, data sources and queries, views and view queries, comments, file uploads, custom emojis and async tasks. The connection only sees content shared with it. OAuth, Notion Agents and Sessions, AI meeting notes, workspace analytics and Admin APIs are not forwarded. Every request must include a Notion-Version header (currently 2026-03-11); the gateway forwards it as sent and Notion returns 400 missing_version without it. Writes and deletes have real effects in your workspace; deleting a block or trashing a page moves it to Notion&#39;s trash.

    Saving, replacing and testing a token only call GET /v1/models and run no paid inference. Chat, text completions and embeddings consume your Nscale credits. A successful check does not verify inference permissions or credit balance; Nscale documents 429 for insufficient credit. Only GET /v1/models, POST /v1/chat/completions, POST /v1/completions and POST /v1/embeddings are forwarded. Completions can stream with SSE.   <p class="mt-5 text-xs leading-relaxed text-navy-500">
    Saving or testing the token reads your monthly limit (GET /1/apps/limits.json) and sends nothing. Each account can send 10,000 messages a month across all its applications; after that Pushover answers 429 until the limit resets on the 1st. Only POST /1/messages.json, POST /1/users/validate.json, GET /1/apps/limits.json and GET /1/receipts/:receipt.json are forwarded. Groups, teams, subscriptions, licensing, Glances, receipt cancellation and the Open Client API are not. Pushover takes the token as a request parameter, so the gateway adds it to the query string as token, replacing any token your Sprite sends. URLs are logged more readily than headers, including on Pushover&#39;s side. Every send is delivered to real devices. Messages are limited to 1,024 characters. Pushover temporarily blocks IP addresses that send many failing (4xx) requests, and every request reaches Pushover from the shared gateway IP, so do not retry a rejected request unchanged.

  <span class="text-xs sm:text-sm font-mono text-right leading-6 text-navy-400">
    2
  </span>

  <div class="flex flex-col gap-2 min-w-0">
    <p class="text-sm font-medium text-navy-700">Configure Sentry</p>

    

    

    

    <p class="text-xs leading-relaxed text-navy-500">
      
      <span>In Sentry, open Personal Tokens (sentry.io/settings/account/api/auth-tokens/) and create a token with only the scopes the Sprite needs. Start with org:read, project:read and event:read. Add project:releases if you need to create releases or deploys. Organization tokens and internal integration tokens also work. Use a token for a US-region organization. Availability varies by organization during rollout. The gateway keeps the credential off your Sprite.</span>
    </p>
  </div>
</li><li class="grid grid-cols-[1.5rem_minmax(0,1fr)] sm:grid-cols-[2rem_minmax(0,1fr)] gap-x-3 sm:gap-x-4 py-4 first:pt-0 last:pb-0">
  <span class="text-xs sm:text-sm font-mono text-right leading-6 text-navy-400">
    3
  </span>

  <div class="flex flex-col gap-2 min-w-0">
    <p class="text-sm font-medium text-navy-700">Grant your Sprite access</p>

    

    

    

    <p class="text-xs leading-relaxed text-navy-500">
      
      <span>Open access settings and turn off Allow all sprites before restricting access by name prefix or labels. If you set both, a Sprite must match both. Save the policy. A connector with no access policy denies all Sprites.</span>
    </p>
  </div>
</li><li class="grid grid-cols-[1.5rem_minmax(0,1fr)] sm:grid-cols-[2rem_minmax(0,1fr)] gap-x-3 sm:gap-x-4 py-4 first:pt-0 last:pb-0">
  <span class="text-xs sm:text-sm font-mono text-right leading-6 text-navy-400">
    4
  </span>

  <div class="flex flex-col gap-2 min-w-0">
    <p class="text-sm font-medium text-navy-700">Test from your Sprite</p>

    

    

    

    <p class="text-xs leading-relaxed text-navy-500">
      
      <span>Run the API Usage example from the connector&#39;s detail page inside an authorized Sprite. The gateway attaches the stored credential; do not copy it into the Sprite.</span>
    </p>
  </div>
</li>
  </ol>

  <p class="mt-5 text-xs leading-relaxed text-navy-500">
    Sentry&#39;s API has no per-request charge. Saving or testing the token reads GET /api/0/, which returns the token&#39;s own scopes. Sentry rate limits each caller per endpoint and answers 429 when exceeded; the X-Sentry-Rate-Limit-* headers are passed back. Sentry asks integrations not to poll: prefer wide queries over tight loops. Read organizations, projects, teams, environments, repositories, issues, events, Discover results, releases, cron check-ins, replays and dashboards. Issue operations and project settings are read-only. The gateway allows writes for releases, deploys, cron monitors and user feedback. It blocks member and invite management, token and DSN management, service hooks, Sentry apps, SCIM and alert rules. Sentry enforces the token&#39;s scopes for each allowed route. Use org:read, project:read and event:read for read-only use. Add project:releases for releases and deploys, alerts:write for cron monitor changes, or project:write for legacy user feedback only if the Sprite needs those operations. Sentry returns 403 when a request exceeds the token&#39;s permissions. This connector talks to sentry.io, the host Sentry documents for organizations whose data is stored in the US. Organizations in the EU region are served from de.sentry.io, and self-hosted Sentry runs on your own host; neither is covered by this connector.
  </p>

  <p class="mt-5 text-xs leading-relaxed text-navy-500">
    Stripe does not charge for API calls. Saving or testing the key reads GET /v1/balance. Catalog writes with a live-mode key update your live products, prices, discounts or tax rates. The connector cannot create or capture payments, refund charges, or change subscriptions. Read balance, balance transactions, customers, payments, refunds, disputes, payouts, invoices, subscriptions, quotes, Checkout Sessions, Payment Links, billing meters and events. Only products, prices, coupons, promotion codes and tax rates accept writes. The gateway blocks Connect endpoints and account-selection headers. Your own account’s records can still reference existing Connect transactions. Within the allowed routes, your key’s Stripe permissions determine what succeeds. Stripe restricted keys (rk_...) carry per-resource None, Read or Write permissions and can be rotated or revoked on their own. Create one with just what the Sprite needs; the key check only requires Balance: Read. A request outside the key&#39;s permissions is refused by Stripe with 403. One connection holds one key, so test mode and live mode are separate connections.

  <p class="mt-5 text-xs leading-relaxed text-navy-500">
    Saving or testing the key reads GET /usage and spends no credits. Basic search costs 1 credit and advanced search costs 2. Extract costs 1 credit per 5 successful URLs, or 2 with extract_depth: &quot;advanced&quot;. Map costs 1 credit per 10 successful pages, or 2 with instructions. Crawl adds the mapping and extraction costs. Research costs 4 to 110 credits with mini and 15 to 250 with pro. Add include_usage: true where supported to see what the request cost. Pay-as-you-go is $0.008 per credit. Only POST /search, POST /extract, POST /crawl, POST /map, POST /research, GET /research/:request_id and GET /usage are forwarded. API key management, organization usage, request logs and feedback are not. Tavily&#39;s rate limits apply per account: 100 requests a minute on the free plan, 1,000 or more on paid plans, with /crawl and /map at 100 a minute, /research at 20 and /usage at 10 per 10 minutes.
